name: g2-fpm-8510-plain
status: confirmed on the lab build; ASLR off; not a universal exploit
md5_lock: select this profile only when the target binary md5 matches; a mismatch invalidates every offset

ps_serializers.note: the default php decode slot is not 16 byte aligned; with session.serialize_handler=php, target ps_serializer_slot and point it at a fake ps_serializer struct in the record

ps_serializer_slot.note: write the fake ps_serializer struct address here; the fake struct is 24 bytes, name at +0, encode at +8, decode at +0x10

decode_call.note: the decode pointer is read from ps_globals+0x160 on every decode, so the write is consumed by the forced END update in the same request

pre_rinit_path.second_decode: multipart END forces update(progress, 1), then initialize and flush run again before RINIT; php_session_normalize_vars zeroes the type words at target+8 and target+24

write.bound: only used_slots + num > 255 rejects; negative used_slots pass
write.value_form: i:<n>; parses an IS_LONG zval, so the written pointer is an arbitrary 64 bit value
write.alignment: target must be 16 byte aligned; ps_serializers[1].decode at 0x14c1b48 is not

record.x_mapping: file byte i maps to ZSTR_VAL + i; ZSTR_VAL = X + 24
record.command_rule: the 0x20 key length byte is the leading space of the shell command; the command is padded to 32 bytes and must end in # so the value text is commented out

libc.note: lab glibc build only; the offset is build and mapping specific; the binary imports no system symbol, only popen, execvp, fork and posix_spawn PLT entries

heap_leak.measured_relation: B0 = K_dest1 - 0x9000 on the fpmboot body with ASLR off; K_dest1 is a fixed body layout constant, so this is not an ASLR capable leak

staticleak.verdict: save path control and static serving proven; M11 encode overread failed; no heap pointer or B0 recovered
staticleak.controls: 21 exchanges against a bound of 20 and 3 of 3 restarts; formal no-save-path, file-not-present and different-sid controls not executed
staticleak.scope: real-target requirements only; no WordPress, MediaWiki or generic upload target was attacked

boot2_candidate.status: lab only; not promoted; no single-process run takes B0 only from HTTP and then sends stage 2

heap_leak.note: no ASLR capable heap leak demonstrated; the static session file route is attempted-negative and the boot2 HTTP leak is a lab-only candidate; the G2 plan needs operator supplied X, P and B0

prerequisites: md5 locked: the target binary must match this profile md5
non PIE target so the ps_serializers table is at a fixed address, or a binary base leak
libc base for system, or a fixed call target that accepts (char *, size_t); the fixed target route is not demonstrated
heap addresses X, P and B0 and the exact record length
upload progress enabled with the forced END update in the same request
the plant request must be the immediately preceding request on the same worker
single shot per plant: RINIT resets BG(unserialize), and the corrupted decode pointer persists until worker restart
with session.serialize_handler=php, target ps_serializer_slot and point it at a fake ps_serializer struct; the php decode slot is not 16 byte aligned
caveats: measured with setarch x86_64 -R; with ASLR on X, P, B0 and the libc base move
a binary md5 mismatch invalidates every offset
the default php serializer decode slot is not 16 byte aligned; the PS(serializer) pointer slot plus a fake ps_serializer struct is the target for that handler
zend_eval_string is not a valid decode target: rsi is ZSTR_LEN and zend_eval_stringl treats a non NULL retval_ptr as a zval and does ZVAL_COPY_VALUE, a wild write for a nonzero length

5.x cannot reuse this geometry: php_unserialize_data is {first, last, first_dtor, last_dtor}, dtor entries use zval *data[1024] with used_slots at +0x2000 and next at +0x2008, the bound is equality, and BG(unserialize) is a struct not a pointer
the fake P and fake B0 must both fall inside the session record buffer; a wrong X either leaves the plant chain in place or crashes var_push
a wrong record length moves the second decode buffer and can crash the second decode
no claim is made for other session savers, opcache, ZTS or shared pools
